prompt: An angle has its vertex at point $B$. One side passes through $A$ and the other side passes through $C$. Which three-letter name is correct for this angle?
hint: In a three-letter angle name, one specific position is reserved for the vertex.

hints.text: In a three-letter angle name, one specific position is reserved for the vertex.
The vertex letter always goes in the MIDDLE. The vertex here is $B$.
With $B$ in the middle, the name is $\angle ABC$ (or $\angle CBA$).

explanation: A three-letter angle name lists a point on one side, then the vertex, then a point on the other side.
The vertex must sit in the middle, and the vertex here is $B$.
So the angle is $\angle ABC$; reading the outer letters backwards, $\angle CBA$, names the same angle.

alternativeExplanations.title: The corner is the middle
steps: Trace the angle with your finger: you come in along one side, TURN at the corner, and go out the other side.
The letter you turn at is the letter that goes in the middle — $B$.
